title: GPU Ops Lodestar — weekly sprint notes (Jun 1–5, 2026)
content:
Purpose: running notes from this week’s infra syncs + standups focused on GPU fleet priming, region hedging, and short-term capacity maneuvers. This is a lightweight working doc — scribbles, triangles of thought, and action items.

Attendees (recurring): Maya (owner), Ethan, Sofia, Noah, Priya, Lila (SRE support), Tom (capacity analytics), Jae (billing signals).

High-level summary:
- Week objective: close the 48–72h priming gap in APAC edge pools and stabilise EU-West spare slots for expected enterprise test on Jun 9.
- Net: queue pressure reduced ~12% after applying transient prewarm rule; tail p99 latency still shows 2–3% spikes tied to cold starts on p3d nodes.
- Risk: increased preemption noise in some us-west2 preemptible configs; flagged for immediate mitigation (see INFRA-4821).

Standup highlights (daily fragments)
- Mon Jun 1: rolled new priming lambda that pre-populates KV caches for frequent prefixes in AR/EN chat models. Experiment id: priming-v7. Observed steady-state token cost +1.8% but effective cold-start reduction of ~37% for small-chat requests.
- Tue Jun 2: APAC region showed higher than expected burst from partner demo (internal). APAC priming ramped to 1.6x baseline — observed queue increase then fallback to slower SLO for background jobs. Action: throttle partner demo in region (Priya).
- Wed Jun 3: Canary of batch multiplier change (x1.1 -> x1.3) shipped to dedicated for low-latency tier. Throughput improved; some jitter in p95 during sustained burst. Ops note: re-evaluate backpressure thresholds.
- Thu Jun 4: SRE reported preemption cascade in us-west2-spot pool at 03:12 UTC — ~120 tasks evicted, auto-fallback hit but rollout of smaller quantized model variants mitigated customer impact. Follow-up: add guard to avoid concurrent large-scale prewarming jobs during cloud maintenance windows.
- Fri Jun 5: Retro + planning: pick a primary mitigator for p99 cold starts (prefix caching vs fast prewarming vs latent warm pool). Consensus: iterate on priming-v7 while prototyping a small warm-pool controller.

Capacity notes and short-term plan
- Current snapshot (end-of-week): global spare capacity ~5.4% across all fleets; EU-West reserve intended for demo week is at 3.1% (target 6–8%). APAC edge spare negative (-0.9%) when factoring partner bursts.
- Immediate actions (next 72h):
  * Top-up EU-West via opportunistic backfill from us-east spare (Tom). Migration plan: soft-drain low-priority slots, rebind high-priority routing to eu-backup class. (Jira: INFRA-4837)
  * Reduce APAC demo throttle rate and reclass partner test traffic to burst queue (Priya).
  * Disable large bulk prewarming jobs during GCP maintenance hours (Maya/Lila).

Preemption and slot churn observations
- Root cause analysis (notes): recent provider maintenance + preemptible eviction pattern correlated with sudden increase in scheduling latency and KV cache misses. Preemption rate up 0.7% week-on-week (small but concentrated in us-west2).
- Quick mitigations implemented: stagger eviction-aware retries, increase backoff jitter, and add proactive checkpoint for long-running sharded sessions. Need longer term: hedged allocation policy for preemptible-heavy workloads.

Experiments and telemetry
- priming-v7: prefix-KV prefill + quick-ttl of 5m. Metrics: cold start rate -37%, token-cost +1.8%, p99 latency improvement ~8% during warm window. Open questions: cost delta sustainable at scale and effect on throughput for batching.
- batch-multiplier-1.3 canary: increased batch size slightly improved GPU utilization by 6% for long-sequence workloads, but variable impact on latency-sensitive routes. Next step: route-aware batching (split by customer tier).
- warm-pool-controller (spike): prototype launched in test cluster. Controller keeps N small warm instances per region for <16-token prefixes. Rough config: N=12 for APAC edge, N=8 for EU-West. Need safety limits to avoid capacity oversubscribe.

Operational playbook tweaks (notes-to-self style)
- Add a soft-preempt policy flag to the deployment manifest so Dedicated customers can opt into hedge vs cost-first behavior.
- Console: expose per-route cold-start rate + priming status in the model dashboard (ask product-console team). Linked idea in confluence page.
- Alerts: create p99-coldstart alert separate from general latency alerts (low-noise, high-signal).

Action items (owners + ETA)
- INFRA-4821 (Ethan) — preemption cascade triage + mitigation patch for staggered retries. ETA: 2026-06-09.
- EU-West top-up runbook (Tom, Maya) — dry-run and then soft migration to eu-backup. ETA: 2026-06-07.
- Partner demo throttle (Priya) — implement rate limit and put into burst queue. ETA: 2026-06-05 (done) — note: confirm partner acknowledges changed SLA.
- Warm-pool safety limits (Sofia) — define region sizing heuristics and safety caps. ETA: 2026-06-11.
- Dashboard card for per-route cold-starts (Maya -> product-console) — create spec and attach to ticket. ETA: 2026-06-18.

Open questions / discussion points
- How aggressive should priming be in memory-constrained edge nodes? Tradeoff: token cost vs latency variance. Opinions: prefer conservative priming for enterprise customer routes, aggressive for self-serve dev tier.
- Should we introduce a paid opt-in for warm pools as a Dedicated add-on? Finance input needed. (Ping: finance-and-legal).

Follow-ups and references
- See INFRA-4821 and related notes in Confluence (pageId=12345678).
- Quick link to the canary dashboard: (internal) /dashboards/gpu-priming/priming-v7.
- PR: infrastructure#987 contains the staggered backoff and fast-fail guard.

Retrospective blurbs (quick, messy)
- What worked: small targeted priming reduced user-visible cold starts without huge cost impact. The warm-pool prototype looks promising for short prefix workloads.
- What didn’t: large bulk prewarms during provider maintenance caused churn; need better maintenance-awareness.
- Weirdness: one EU-West node reported a steady 3s p99 even under low CPU — likely network hickup; ticketed to SRE for packet-capture window.

Notes-to-self: keep this doc as the working log for next 2 sprints then formalise into playbook. Add examples of priming-config JSON and an RBAC note for who can trigger top-ups.

Appendix (quick metrics snapshot)
- global spare capacity: 5.4%
- eu-west reserve: 3.1% (target 6–8%)
- apac spare (edge): -0.9% (after recent partner burst)
- p99 cold-start reduction (priming-v7): ~37%
- token cost impact (priming-v7): +1.8%

If you’re reading this and want to edit: add your notes inline, tag with @owner, and link to any relevant Jira/PRs.

---
Recorded by Maya Patel (GPU Ops lead) — quick edit 2026-06-08 to reflect completed partner throttle and updated EU-West plan.
